      <title>Race to replant five South African baobabs after export blocked</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said <a href="https://www.unfpa.org/swp2026">the report</a> by the UN Population Fund (<a href="https://www.unfpa.org/latest?_gl=1*qgl8yd*_up*MQ..*_gs*MQ..&amp;gclid=Cj0KCQiAtvXXBhC2ARIsAJc8SUT_aKqck2yVoC8vNqJ6FDghCWHDwCXcKD3yGJ9fmgqTGSh0z0LaYAcaAvlMEALw_wcB&amp;gbraid=0AAAAAoaU5jLrFra9lcVEXtmHPvgYu0nsj">UNFPA</a>) published on Thursday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court</link>
      <description><p>A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza</p><p>Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay</a>, if the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/15/myanmar-rohingya-genocide-icj">court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide</a> against the Rohingya.</p><p>The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/us-sanctions-icj-judges-myanmar-genocide-ruling-israel-gaza-court">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans</link>
      <description><p>Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans</p><p>The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.</p><p>The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/mar/17/egypt-eu-deal-refugees-mediterranean">promised by Ursula von der Leyen</a>, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/european-commission-accused-sugarcoating-figures-egypt-loans">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda</link>
      <description><p>Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’</p><p>Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.</p><p>The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/26/meps-back-plans-for-return-hubs-raising-fears-of-human-rights-black-holes">newly agreed returns law</a> that allows<em> </em>people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/eu-states-immigration-return-hubs-rwanda">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/pete-hegseth-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-military</link>
      <description><p>Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago</p><p>Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.</p><p>Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/18/pete-hegseth-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-military">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas  </p><p>The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.</p><p>The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/datacentres-to-create-70-more-carbon-emissions-by-2030-iea-report-warns">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Stories revealing Pauline Hanson’s US trip with Gina Rinehart and the systemic betrayal of Kardell Lomas before her death recognised</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Guardian Australia journalists have won two Walkley awards, one for a story about the systemic betrayal of a woman who was killed by her partner, and another for an exclusive story that revealed Pauline Hanson had travelled to the US with mining billionaire Gina Rinehart.</p><p>Investigative reporter Sarah Martin won the award for print/text news report for her <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2025/dec/30/pauline-hanson-travelled-to-us-on-gina-rineharts-private-jet-to-attend-cpac">exclusive story that revealed </a>the One Nation leader and her chief of staff, James Ashby, travelled with Rinehart on the mining magnate’s Gulfstream 700 on 27 October last year.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/19/guardian-australia-takes-home-two-walkley-awards-for-excellence-in-journalism">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Britain understood to have made concessions on youth mobility scheme as negotiations on wider deal continue</p><p>British and EU negotiators have provisionally agreed to allow 100,000 young EU citizens to come to the UK every year under a new mobility scheme, as negotiations on the UK-EU reset talks go “down to the wire”.</p><p>Tensions in Brussels remained high on Thursday afternoon as ambassadors began crunch talks on the latest draft of the wider agreement, with sources confirming both sides were still battling over the exact nature of the UK’s role in shaping future European food and farming rules, in a second part of the deal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/19/uk-eu-reset-talks-andy-burnham-food-farming-tuition-fees">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:45:09 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Spotlight on France</category><title>Podcast: Living on the breadline, France's 35-hour week and a divisive tax</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/podcasts/spotlight-on-france/20261119-podcast-living-on-minimum-wage-smic-35-hour-working-week-france-second-biggest-tax-csg</link><description>
The French government's decision to raise the minimum wage has failed to satisfy protesters struggling to make ends meet amid the cost-of-living crisis. Also, did the introduction of the 35-hour working week actually help reduce unemployment? The evidence is mixed. And a look at the history of France's second-largest tax, the CSG, and why it's dividing politicians. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/8a275ba4-e41c-11f1-8716-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/episode-spotlight-on-france-episode-153-light-blue.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">da07160a-e41c-11f1-9424-dd481487d627</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:19:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sarah Elzas</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France raises bird flu alert to highest level as infections spread across Europe</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261119-france-raises-bird-flu-alert-to-highest-level-as-infections-spread-across-europe</link><description>
France is raising its avian flu alert to the highest level from Friday, bringing new restrictions on poultry movements as authorities seek to contain the spread of the virus. The decision comes amid a rise in infections among wild birds across Europe, particularly along migration routes crossing France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eff2afda-e3f7-11f1-a0c0-bdb47d3d53b3</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:12:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/42222ee2-1fab-11eb-b845-005056bf87d6/w:1024/p:16x9/6850244_699464634-000-ft7gh.png">© GAIZKA IROZ / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-france-rejects-absurd-russian-claims-of-direct-involvement-in-ukraine-war</link><description>
The French government on Tuesday dismissed Russian accusations that France is directly involved in the war in Ukraine, following an RFI investigation which revealed a small number of French soldiers have been carrying out training and equipment maintenance missions on Ukrainian territory. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ffdd448e-e346-11f1-831b-65a66bd770f6</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:39:09 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/746c6ae0-4ac3-11f1-935e-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000-89T43XG.jpg">AFP - BERTRAND GUAY</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French interior minister accused of 'exaggerating' police protest injury figures</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-french-interior-minister-accused-of-exaggerating-police-protest-injury-figures</link><description>
A group of lawyers have called for an investigation into French Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez who they accuse of "spreading false information" about the number of injuries suffered by law enforcement officers since the start of the current protest movement, which they say was used "to justify a disproportionate use of force" against high school protesters.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">294b16e6-e335-11f1-af18-6757e9484dfb</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:09:32 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/0622d13a-dad5-11f1-9395-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6RB3AC.jpg">AFP - SEBASTIEN BOZON</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'We weren't afraid of the future': France's student protests today and in May '68</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-we-weren-t-afraid-of-the-future-france-s-student-protests-today-and-in-may-68</link><description>
As students across France continue demonstrating against conditions in schools, the movement has drawn inevitable comparisons with the biggest student protests in the country's history – those of May 1968. While this date remains a rallying cry for many young French people, they are calling for change in a world that has altered profoundly in the past 58 years.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">457488e8-dceb-11f1-88f8-bd68fc553891</guid><pubDate>Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:01:49 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/165d86c2-0db3-11ea-96a7-005056a9aa4d/w:1024/p:16x9/000_v48m0_0.jpg">© JACQUES MARIE / AFP </source><dc:creator>Jessica Phelan</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Lower turnout at latest French cost-of-living protests, but anger still raw</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261118-lower-turnout-at-latest-french-cost-of-living-protests-but-anger-still-raw</link><description>
Tens of thousands of people demonstrated across France on Tuesday in a fresh nationwide public sector strike over pay and the cost of living. Although turnout was lower than at previous protests, anger remained strong – with many demonstrators also voicing fears about the far right coming to power in the 2027 presidential election.

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8f4305e2-dd0b-11f1-ad88-012109f6bc5c</guid><pubDate>Wed, 11 Nov 2026 06:05:01 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12bc0fa4-1086-11ea-8502-005056a99247/w:1024/p:16x9/2012-11-11T144200Z_94089871_GM1E8BB1QZK01_RTRMADP_3_FRANCE.JPG">REUTERS/Pascal Rosssignol</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students demonstrate solidarity in the fight for better schools</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-students-demonstrate-solidarity-in-the-fight-for-better-schools</link><description>
It began as a protest over crumbling classrooms and missing teachers, but France's student movement is now challenging the political establishment to give young people more of a say in decisions about their future. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f19af422-dc5f-11f1-a6cf-03231484c166</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 21:55:52 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/37f55a2a-d6b6-11f1-94f8-d18c5759e759/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26306393160391.jpg">AP Photo/Nicolas Garriga - Nicolas Garriga</source><dc:creator>Alison Hird</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French student protests continue amid deadlock over education reforms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261110-french-student-protests-continue-amid-deadlock-over-education-reforms</link><description>
Students and teachers are planning a new day of strikes and demonstrations on Tuesday, as talks with the government remain deadlocked, nearly two months after the start of protests by high school and university students.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">37288fa8-dcd4-11f1-aace-7ff548d44c0a</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 06:59:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/29cb24b4-c8b7-11f1-9aa3-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-15T145022Z-1497667603-RC2N3OANCMHS-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">© Stephane Mahe/Reuters</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Anthropic valued at $2tn as shares begin trading after record-breaking IPO – business live</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/19/anthropic-float-stock-market-nasdaq-raises-81bn-record-ipo-latest-news-updates</link>
      <description><p>Rolling coverage of Anthropic’s IPO, and the latest economic and financial news</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/anthropic-public-trading-ipo">Anthropic to begin public trading at $1.5tn valuation after largest ever IPO</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2026/nov/19/our-ai-future-stateside">Outages, spies, and trillion-dollar IPOs: is this our AI future? – Stateside with Kai and Carter</a></p></li></ul><p><br></p><p><strong>Anthropic </strong>needs to grow into its $1.5tn valuation, argues <strong>Kathleen Brooks,</strong> research director at <strong>XTB:</strong></p><p>Anthropic’s triumphant IPO and its trillion dollar plus valuation is more typical of a mature company that has a history of strong fundamentals. Anthropic could not be more different. It has generated strong revenue growth, but only in the short term, added to this, it is still unprofitable.</p><p>Anthropic is another major tech company that requires investors to have a lot of faith about the future generation of revenues based on technology that will change the world. It seems like plenty are willing to give it that faith, and it is having a huge impact on the broader market today.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/19/anthropic-float-stock-market-nasdaq-raises-81bn-record-ipo-latest-news-updates">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Union leaders from 19 countries urge reassessment of ties to Amazon, citing company’s poor record on worker rights</p><p>More than 30 labor union leaders from 19 countries are calling on governments to review their public contracts with Amazon and Amazon Web Services, citing the company’s poor record on worker rights and collective bargaining, in an<a href="https://uniglobalunion.org/wp-content/uploads/Amazon-procurement-letter-embargoed-until-nov-19.pdf"> open letter</a> published on Thursday.</p><p>“Amazon’s consistent record of disrespect for workers’ fundamental rights should disqualify it from being awarded public contracts – its behaviour is fundamentally inconsistent with the shared democratic values of our countries,” the union leaders wrote.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/labor-unions-amazon-contracts-open-letter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Company insists Alice Huang, who is accused of being a Chinese spy, left business in late 2025</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/elon-musk-tech-execs-open-letter-jensen-huang-return-nvidia-ceo">Elon Musk joins 165,000 others calling for Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/16/ai-sell-off-resumes-jensen-huang-discusses-comeback-nvidia-ceo-dollar-stock-markets-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Megaspeed International, the company linked to the downfall of the Nvidia chief, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/jensen-huang">Jensen Huang</a>, says it is a “legitimate and lawful business” and has announced that its director, who allegedly had an affair with Jensen Huang, left the business in late 2025.</p><p>The Singapore-based cloud computing company on the weekend said it was “aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/megaspeed-company-breaks-slience-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A layoff and a leap of faith convinced Katie Teixeira she had what it takes to run her own business</p><p>In 2010, Katie Teixeira adopted a kitten found all alone in an abandoned house. </description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <title>Fifa sparks tension with demand for tax-free status in UK for Women’s World Cup</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/fifa-demand-tax-free-status-in-uk-womens-world-cup-2035-government</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>It also wants exchange-rate fees exemption for 2035</p></li><li><p>Fifa at loggerheads with UK’s four FAs and government</p></li></ul><p>Fifa is at loggerheads with the UK’s government and four football associations over the world governing body’s demands for tax-free status and exemptions from exchange-rate fees at the 2035 Women’s World Cup.</p><p>The UK bid to host the tournament is due to be ratified at an extraordinary Fifa congress in Zurich on Monday and the Guardian has learned there is tension behind the scenes over many of Fifa’s requirements, which multiple sources involved in the discussions have indicated will not be met.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/fifa-demand-tax-free-status-in-uk-womens-world-cup-2035-government">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/football-daily-fifa-presidential-election</link>
      <description><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up"><strong>Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!</strong></a></p><p>Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/games/2026/nov/18/grand-theft-auto-vi-gta-6-review-playstation-rockstar">“most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world”</a>, football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat.</p><p>When I first saw the photo in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/cincinnati-manchester-united-pochettino-football-daily-newsletter">yesterday’s Football Daily</a>, I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner.</p><p>That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others).</p><p><em><strong>This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version,<a href="https://preview.gutools.co.uk/info/2016/jan/05/the-fiver-email-sign-up"> </a><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/info/2022/nov/14/football-daily-email-sign-up">just visit this page and follow the instructions</a>.</strong></em> </p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/football-daily-fifa-presidential-election">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/premier-league-vote-new-rules-financial-indemnity-lawsuits</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Individual indemnity extended for potential lawsuits</p></li><li><p>Key figures may be named in action over Manchester City</p></li></ul><p>Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.</p><p>A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/premier-league-vote-new-rules-financial-indemnity-lawsuits">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview</link>
      <description><p>Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham</p><p>The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.</p><p>Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/gonzalo-garcia-fulham-spain-premier-leaue-interview">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/danny-kelly-death-football-radio</link>
      <description><p>The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly</p><p>It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/oct/30/premierleague-arsenal">who prods it home</a> and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.</p><p>But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is <a href="https://www.facebook.com/THFCOnThisDay/videos/i-love-football-stan-i-love-itrest-in-peace-danny-kelly-/3113435382350217/">such a brilliant piece of radio</a>. From one of the absolute greats.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/danny-kelly-death-football-radio">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/football/football">Football</category>

      <title>Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/syria-womens-football</link>
      <description><p>A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty</p><p>In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.</p><p>Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/syria-womens-football">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/mls-salary-release-lionel-messi-spent-per-point</link>
      <description><p>How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight</p><p>Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.</p><p>Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/mls-salary-release-lionel-messi-spent-per-point">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Croix Bethune, Trinity Rodman and the Rowdy Audi crowd are among the factors that could swing Saturday’s final </p><p>This year’s NWSL Championship blends recurring themes with some newness. For the familiar: the Washington Spirit are in the final for the third straight year, hoping the third time’s the charm after back-to-back 1-0 defeats in their past two attempts. Slightly familiar, too, is Kansas City Current playing the championship game at Washington’s Audi Field, where they lost the final to Portland in 2022 and where they will contend again Saturday.</p><p>For the novelty? Neither Kansas City nor Washington, despite their modern dominance in the NWSL table, have won the championship since 2021 (when Washington won).       <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/chelsea-paris-saint-germain-womens-champions-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Chelsea were made to work hard for three Champions League points against a resilient Paris Saint-Germain side but their patience paid off, Veerle Buurman squeezing the ball in at the near post to put them, temporarily at least, at the top of the table in the league phase.</p><p>Buurman had stolen the show in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Chelsea’s defeat of Manchester City</a> at the weekend, coming on 12 minutes in and nullifying Khadija Shaw’s threat to be named player of the match, and she was the hero under the lights with Chelsea doing everything but score prior to her goal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/chelsea-paris-saint-germain-womens-champions-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/leicester-city-bc-game-porn-star-eva-elfie-sponsorship</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Cryptocurrency casino made Eva Elfie a brand ambassador</p></li><li><p>Club end deal early citing ‘differing commercial priorities’</p></li></ul><p>Leicester City have ditched their front-of-shirt sponsor, BC Game, after the cryptocurrency casino’s partnership with a porn actor sparked a fan backlash. BC Game, an offshore company registered in Belize <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/08/premier-league-clubs-sponsorship-advertising-deals-unlicensed-gambling-companies-uk-government">that is unlicensed to operate in the UK</a>, had been Leicester’s main sponsor since 2024.</p><p>This month BC Game named Eva Elfie a brand ambassador, leading the Foxes Trust, Leicester’s supporters’ trust, to highlight the “devastating impacts” caused by gambling and pornography. On Wednesday the club said they prematurely ended their agreement with the online betting firm after they “recognised our differing commercial priorities”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/leicester-city-bc-game-porn-star-eva-elfie-sponsorship">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Controversial breaks were financial boon for broadcasters</p></li><li><p>Fifa flags possible benefits but says no decision made</p></li></ul><p>Fifa’s tender documents for TV rights for the 2030 World Cup include a provision for broadcasters<strong> </strong>to sell adverts during hydration breaks in a strong indication <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/jun/26/fifa-unites-the-world-in-anger-at-hydration-breaks-aka-ad-breaks">the controversial ­stoppages</a> will be retained.</p><p>A three-minute break midway through each half was introduced for the first time at all 104 matches at last summer’s World Cup in the interests of player welfare, a radical move that also provided a commercial boon for broadcasters, particularly the rights holders in the United States, Fox Sports and Telemundo.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/fifa-hydration-breaks-2030-world-cup-tv-right-documents">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry</p><p>The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but.</p><p>Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/netflix-fox-2030-world-cup-television-rights">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst</link>
      <description><p>The role of full-back has changed massively in recent years. We analyse how all 20 sides are approaching the position</p><p>By <a href="https://theanalyst.com/">Opta Analyst</a></p><p>Overlapping. Underlapping. Inverted. Traditional. The role of full-back has evolved dramatically. Once a defensive-first position that provided some auxiliary attacking support, the role has developed into something far more multifaceted.</p><p>Just ask right-back Ben White, who – with Riccardo Calafiori on the left – has been an important figure in Arsenal’s superb start to the campaign. Talking a few years ago, he said: “Playing full-back the way [Mikel Arteta] wants is completely different to any other manager. To play full-back for him, you’ve got to be a centre-midfielder, a centre-back, a winger and a No 10.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/premier-league-teams-full-backs-opta-analyst">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Jack Grealish recalls a golden age of mavericks – but football has moved on</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on</link>
      <description><p>Everton forward has magical talent and popularity to burn, but has come up against hard reality of the modern game</p><p>Thomas Tuchel has never called up the player he once claimed to love “everything about”. The reason for Jack Grealish’s omission from Tuchel’s first England squad in March 2025 was given as “he simply has no rhythm”.</p><p>Catch a falling star? Last month Grealish <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/oct/29/jack-grealish-axed-everton-breach-club-discipline-newcastle-caraboao-cup">was suspended by Everton</a> for three matches after “a breach of club discipline”. Suggestions his loan from Manchester City might be cancelled were calmed by David Moyes. Last week, Grealish played in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Derby before issuing an Instagram statement: “I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.” Amid tabloid tales of karaoke nights and extended socialising, how close is the former boy wonder, now 31, to blowing it?</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/jack-grealish-recalls-a-golden-age-of-mavericks-but-football-has-moved-on">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘When I walked for Burberry I met Kanye West’: the two lives of Bromley footballer Omar Sowunmi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west</link>
      <description><p>Full-time defender and part-time model, the 31-year-old is happy to shine a light on both sides of his dual career</p><p>“I was walking down the street one day and someone came up to me and said: ‘I think you should be a model,’” the Bromley defender Omar Sowunmi says. He was already living out many people’s dreams as a professional footballer but was able to assume an alter ego in the world of fashion. There are few parallels between the grind of lower-league football and Milan fashion week but the 31-year-old is adept in both worlds.</p><p>Sowunmi’s dual career mixes trips to Doncaster with visits to Paris. On Saturday Bromley travel to Reading under their new manager, Karl Robinson, as they attempt to move off the bottom of League One and the centre-back is clear where his focus lies even after his chance encounter with a model agency employee expanded his horizons.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/18/omar-sowunmi-bromley-footballer-model-kanye-west">Continue reading...</a></description>

Appelant les alliés de Kiev réunis à Berlin, dont les États-Unis, à faire le "maximum" pour lui livrer "maintenant" les moyens de défense antiaériens dont elle a besoin, le président français a demandé jeudi à "rouvrir la question de l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Otan".

Guillaume Grallet, rédacteur en chef tech et sciences au Point et chroniqueur à France 24, auteur de Pionniers, voyage aux frontières de l’intelligence artificielle, décrypte cette opération.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3edcbdf4-e44b-11f1-87cd-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-183015-183549-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/3edcbdf4-e44b-11f1-87cd-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-183015-183549-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c1c72ac6-e44e-11f1-80d3-09e8069e15bd</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 19:23:52 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Stéphanie ANTOINE</dc:creator></item><item><category>Élément Terre, la quotidienne</category><title>COP31: l'avenir de l'agriculture en question</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/%C3%A9l%C3%A9ment-terre-la-quotidienne/20261119-cop31-l-avenir-de-l-agriculture-en-question</link><description>
Le réchauffement climatique est l'un des principaux facteurs d'aggravation de l'insécurité alimentaire dans le monde. L'agriculture mondiale est victime de ce phénomène mais l'aggrave aussi puisqu'elle est responsable de près d'un quart des émissions mondiales de gaz à effet de serre et contribue à affaiblir le puit carbone des sols. Pour la FAO transformer l'agriculture pour qu'elle soit moins émettrice et garantisse la sécurité alimentaire mondiale doit être la priorité des priorités.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/374526da-e446-11f1-81d6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-cf4f3fbe.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/374526da-e446-11f1-81d6-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-cf4f3fbe.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">22db07f2-e449-11f1-9875-0b506a75bb67</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 18:43:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Audrey RACINE</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Au procès Zecler, prison ferme requise contre les policiers, la question du racisme réintroduite</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/info-en-continu/20261119-au-proc%C3%A8s-zecler-prison-ferme-requise-contre-les-policiers-la-question-du-racisme-r%C3%A9introduite</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9e401aba-e429-11f1-bd39-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/miniahaiti.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9e401aba-e429-11f1-bd39-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/miniahaiti.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">bf0a4f9a-e429-11f1-ba16-094ec6f3ff28</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 15:28:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Sommet de Shenzhen : Vladimir Poutine, le grand humilié ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261119-sommet-shenzhen-vladimir-poutine-grand-humili%C3%A9-xi-jinping-trump-apec</link><description>

La Birmanie a commis un génocide à l'encontre de sa minorité rohingya, a déclaré jeudi la Cour internationale de justice dans une décision historique, ordonnant que les réfugiés puissent regagner leur foyer en toute sécurité et prévoyant le versement d'indemnisations.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/46805a48-e428-11f1-93c2-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-150131-150656-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/46805a48-e428-11f1-93c2-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-150131-150656-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4ba605f4-e428-11f1-8bc6-b192d330686e</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:57:04 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Haïti : la stratégie de Bukele reçoit un soutien populaire</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261119-ha%C3%AFti-la-strat%C3%A9gie-de-bukele-re%C3%A7oit-un-soutien-populaire</link><description>
Des milliers de personnes ont défilé dans les rues de Port-au-Prince, mardi, pour soutenir les soldats salvadoriens engagés dans la lutte contre les gangs en Haïti. Les explications de Frantz Duval, rédacteur en chef du quotidien Le Nouvelliste.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/554ec0be-e428-11f1-b053-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261118-210630-211204-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/554ec0be-e428-11f1-b053-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261118-210630-211204-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5a2e4924-e428-11f1-8845-7f9fae826d1f</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:53:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Face à face</category><title>Primaire du centre et de la droite : Édouard Philippe, sous pression, refuse toujours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/face-%C3%A0-face/20261119-primaire-du-centre-et-de-la-droite-%C3%A9douard-philippe-sous-pression-refuse-toujours</link><description>
Une primaire de la droite et du centre pourraient avoir lieu fin janvier après une première réunion entre les équipes de Gabriel Attal, David Lisnard et Bruno Retailleau. Édouard Philippe, malgré la pression de ses concurrents, refuse toujours d'y participer. Pourra t-il résister ? Ce refus peut-il lui coûter cher alors que David Lisnard, le maire de Cannes, est en dynamique dans les sondages ?

Écologistes et Insoumis pourraient entamer ⁠prochainement des discussions ​sur les modalités de la "coalition autour de la candidature de Jean-Luc Mélenchon" évoquée par la dirigeante verte Marine Tondelier en vue de l'élection présidentielle, a-t-on appris jeudi dans l'entourage de cette dernière.

"Embarqué par les algorithmes", le fondateur du canal Télégram "femmeblancherie", jugé aux côtés de six autres prévenus, a témoigné d'une haine tenace envers les femmes mercredi devant le tribunal de Paris lors du premier procès d'ampleur de la mouvance masculiniste.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c1494e8-e424-11f1-8475-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-143136-144336-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2c1494e8-e424-11f1-8475-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-143136-144336-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">311f647c-e424-11f1-baec-2fe1eca68965</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:23:27 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Royaume-Uni : comment l’IA transforme le système d’asile des migrants</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261119-royaume-uni-comment-l-ia-transforme-le-syst%C3%A8me-d-asile-des-migrants</link><description>
Le Royaume-Uni utilise de plus en plus l’intelligence artificielle dans son système migratoire, notamment pour traiter les demandes d’asile. Mais erreurs, manque de contrôle humain et opacité inquiètent les organisations de défense des droits numériques. Stella Elgersma, journaliste chez InfoMigrants, décrypte ces nouvelles technologies et les risques qu’elles font peser sur les droits des personnes migrantes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/35e156d2-e424-11f1-a164-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-134705-135201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/35e156d2-e424-11f1-a164-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261119-134705-135201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3b1bcdbc-e424-11f1-8b03-2d1f8cde3423</guid><pubDate>Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:22:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Mardi politique</category><title>Jad Zahab : la France n'est "plus une nation libre car nous sommes endettés"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/mardi-politique/20261119-jad-zahab-la-france-n-est-plus-une-nation-libre-car-nous-sommes-endett%C3%A9s</link><description>
Jad Zahab, porte-parole de Gabriel Attal, estime que "Gabriel Attal a le programme le plus radical". Concernant la crise du pouvoir d'achat, sujet qui selon lui sera au coeur de la campagne, il affirme que "les Français ne demandent pas à être aidés mais à vivre dignement de leur travail".
